_readme: The knowledge pack. It is added to every LLM prompt and used by the rules engine. Every item has an ID and a source. Edit this file, not the code. Items marked to_be_vetted must be confirmed by their owner before the app is used for real brands.

guardrails.text: Reminder messages with an assuring tone get a higher CTA rate than urgent ones; urgent tone in reminders reads as nagging.
guardrails.source: Vi RBM Playbook, CPaaS Edition (C1 External), guardrail: tone x intent

guardrails.text: BFSI, insurance and healthcare informational and transactional messages perform best in a formal tone.
guardrails.source: Vi RBM Playbook, CPaaS Edition (C1 External)

guardrails.text: Promotional pushes are the exception to G1: urgent tone drives action where the intent itself is time-bound.
guardrails.source: Vi RBM Playbook, CPaaS Edition (C1 External)

guardrails.text: Regional-language text builds trust and eases absorption; a CTA in the regional language lifts clicks further. Tune tone and idiom, do not only translate.
guardrails.source: Vi RBM Playbook, CPaaS Edition (C1 External), guardrail: language

guardrails.text: Match CTA specificity to the funnel stage: generic CTAs (Know More) suit exploration; specific CTAs (Book Now, Pay Now) suit decision stage and pair with urgency; for high-commitment categories (loans, insurance) generic CTAs such as Check Eligibility are preferred.
guardrails.source: Vi RBM Playbook, CPaaS Edition (C1 External), guardrail: CTA design

guardrails.text: Segmentation, frequency control and structured A/B testing protect read rate at scale; broad blasts to uninterested users are the biggest driver of spam complaints.
guardrails.source: Vi RBM Playbook, CPaaS Edition (C1 External), foundations

guardrails.text: Use decision CTAs (Book Now, Pay Now) only once value and urgency have both been communicated.
guardrails.source: Vi RBM Playbook, CPaaS Edition (C1 External), rule of thumb

guardrails.text: Industry by tone quick reference: BFSI formal; ecommerce urgent; retail and healthcare assuring.
guardrails.source: Vi RBM Playbook, CPaaS Edition (C1 External), cheat sheet

platform_facts.text: A rich card can hold media (image, GIF, video, PDF), title text, description text and suggested replies and actions. At least one of media, title or description is required.
platform_facts.source: Google RCS for Business: Rich cards (developers.google.com), checked 2026-10

platform_facts.text: Media height is short (112 DP), medium (168 DP) or tall (264 DP). If the media does not match the chosen height it is zoomed and centre-cropped; a thumbnail can be specified to control what shows.
platform_facts.source: Google RCS for Business: Rich cards, checked 2026-10

platform_facts.text: Selecting the media preview or thumbnail opens a full-screen view of the media; it does not follow the card's button link.
platform_facts.source: Google RCS for Business: Rich cards, checked 2026-10

do_not_assert: That the notification preview shows exactly N characters of the title or description (the character limit is not verified). Say 'the preview may cut the text' only.
Any claim about how an operator, handset or Google client changed behaviour between two periods.
Any causal claim about visits, orders or conversion: the performance sheet holds none of these.
